events.what_changed: Art. 18 (wording of Ley 7234 of 1991) annulled a fraudulently obtained naturalisation where the person gave false data or had been convicted before of an offence in art. 15(2)-(3). Ley 10508 extends this to the new art. 15(4) offences (intentional crimes with more than 3 years' prison in the last 10 years). This is a nullity tied to the grant, which the indicator excludes. Post-grant convictions still do not affect nationality (Const. art. 16).
events.passage: Artículo 18- Es nula, de pleno derecho, la naturalización que fraudulentamente haya obtenido un extranjero con violación de los requisitos que dispone esta ley. En consecuencia, en cualquier momento en que se compruebe que al solicitar u obtener la carta, el individuo naturalizado suministró algún dato falso o fue condenado antes por un delito de los que señalan los incisos 2), 3) y 4) del artículo 15

answers.implementation_then_now: I found no documented case, before or after 2023, of a naturalised Costa Rican losing nationality over a conviction handed down after naturalisation. In 2024 the Assembly sent bill 23.800 back to first debate because it would have stripped nationality from naturalised persons who commit crimes. Deputies called it unconstitutional under art. 16 (El Observador, March 2024). It was enacted only as the pre-grant eligibility and nullity reform (Ley 10508). The rating is therefore 'Effectively Always' on both dates.

events.instrument: Ley N.º 10508, Reforma de los artículos 15 y 18 de la Ley 1155 (Alcance N.º 147 a La Gaceta N.º 158)
events.what_changed: Adds a new bar to naturalisation for anyone convicted by final judgment, in Costa Rica or abroad, of an intentional crime with more than 3 years' prison in the last ten years. It also suspends the application while criminal proceedings are pending. The residence pathway remains but has a tighter eligibility condition.

En caso de que la persona gestionante tenga procesos judiciales penales pendientes... se tomarán las medidas legales pertinentes vía administrativa, a efectos de ordenar la suspensión del trámite

answers.implementation_then_now: La Nación (2025) reports official TSE data. Naturalisation letters averaged about 5,300 a year from 2016, peaked at 6,277 in 2023 and reached 5,541 in 2024. The pathway therefore worked on both dates. The same report documents a shift: resolution once took about six months, now averages over a year, sometimes 18 months, with almost 8,000 applications pending for lack of staff. The rating is 'Usually' on both dates, with growing delays by 2025–26.

practice_sources.title: ¿Cómo se naturalizan los extranjeros en Costa Rica? (La Nación)

answers.sourcing_note: Const. art. 14 was read on SINALEVI, unchanged since 1987/1999. Ley 1155 art. 11 and the Ley 10508 amendment were read in Bufete transcriptions of the official text; the 2023 version was rebuilt by removing inciso 4. The TSE Reglamento PDF could not be read, and no 2023–2025 amendment to it was found in searches.
answers.notes: The answer stays 'Yes'. I chose 'not the same' because a dated statute (Ley 10508, in force 28 Aug 2024) added a criminal-record bar and a suspension rule to the pathway. If the MRD treats only the yes/no existence of the pathway as the protection, the 'no change' option would apply instead. Even before 10508, art. 11(4) already excluded people tried for intentional crimes during their stay. The La Nación figures do not break down applicants by permit type, so 'economic migrants' is inferred.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 but they are not the same

events.what_changed: Adds the new criminal-record bar. It exempts recognised refugees, stateless persons and asylees whose earlier conviction was known when protection was granted, unless they commit intentional crimes during or after the procedure. The pathway itself was unchanged (Yes on both dates); its conditions for humanitarian migrants changed.

answers.implementation_then_now: Recognised refugees and declared stateless persons can naturalise, and La Nación (2025) lists the stateless/stateless-refugee route as one in use. Access stays narrow because few claims are decided. La Prensa (July 2025) reports about 190,000 pending Nicaraguan claims against roughly 16,000 recognitions, with the DGME director putting decisions at two to three years. The backlog was already severe around 2022–23. I found no TSE figures on refugee naturalisations for either period, so I rate 'Sometimes' on both dates.

events.what_changed: Adds a new criminal-record bar to all naturalisations: intentional crime, more than 3 years' prison, last 10 years, in Costa Rica or abroad. Marriage-based applicants must have no art. 15 conviction, so the bar reaches them. The family routes in Const. arts. 14(5) and 17 are unchanged.

answers.implementation_then_now: La Nación (2025) quotes the Registro Civil director: residence and marriage to a Costa Rican are the two main routes. Marriage needs only two years and the legal bond, with no exam. Total grants were 6,277 in 2023 and 5,541 in 2024, so the routes worked on both dates. Waiting times rose from about six months to over a year, up to 18 months, by 2025. The rating is 'Usually' on both dates.
